s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic symmetric hand swelling and erythema with intermittent exacerbations
salient_findings: 15-month history of swelling and redness of hands
Chronic joint pain in hands and back
History of intravenous drug use
Painless, symmetric swelling of both hands
Bilateral dorsal hand erythema and edema
Small-vessel ectasia and minimal perivascular lymphocytes on punch biopsy
key_facts: 35-year-old woman
Bipolar I disorder
Chronic joint pain
Occupational exposure to pool chemicals
No improvement with glove use
Prior treatments with topical mupirocin and emollients were unsuccessful
History of injecting heroin, buprenorphine, suboxone, and morphine
No tourniquet use during intravenous drug use
Intravenous drug use ceased three years prior to current symptoms
Symmetric swelling of both hands
Persistent hand and foot edema during pregnancy
Normal ejection fraction on echocardiogram
Negative antinuclear antibody, extractable nuclear antigen panel, and rheumatoid factor
Mildly elevated creatine kinase and aldolase
Normal creatinine levels, hepatic function tests, and hepatitis panels

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic symmetric hand swelling and erythema with intermittent exacerbations, consistent with scleroderma symptoms

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic Fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic joint pain and symmetric hand swelling, consistent with eosinophilic fasciitis symptoms

shortlist.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic joint pain and symmetric hand swelling, consistent with Sjögren's syndrome symptoms

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic joint pain and symmetric hand swelling, consistent with rheumatoid arthritis symptoms

shortlist.label: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic joint pain and symmetric hand swelling, consistent with complex regional pain syndrome symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's history of symmetric swelling, chronic joint pain, and skin changes, combined with the biopsy findings of small-vessel ectasia and minimal perivascular lymphocytes, are consistent with Eosinophilic Fasciitis. The lack of response to topical treatments and the presence of mildly elevated creatine kinase and aldolase also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy findings do not show the characteristic skin thickening and fibrosis of Scleroderma.

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the characteristic dry eyes and dry mouth of Sjögren's Syndrome, and the laboratory tests do not show positive antinuclear antibody or extractable nuclear antigen panel.

rejected.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory tests do not show the characteristic positive rheumatoid factor and erosive joint changes of Rheumatoid Arthritis.

rejected.label: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the characteristic burning pain and trophic changes of Complex Regional Pain Syndrome, and the biopsy findings do not show the characteristic nerve damage.
